corrections.reason: Putting numbers up to 50 in order depends on knowing the counting sequence up to 50 (which number comes next, and where each number sits on a number line or hundred chart). That is taught in g1-count-50, which is not listed. It is a direct need, not covered by any other listed prerequisite, so it should be added.

The skill is solving stories up to 50 with pictures, number lines, and equations, and finding the missing number. A kid can do this without mental math strategies for sums to 20, so g1-mental-math-20 is not a true prerequisite and should be removed. The remaining prerequisites are needed: the inverse relationship for finding missing numbers (g1-add-sub-properties), composing and decomposing tens and ones to work with numbers to 50 (g1-compose-decompose-50), and the story-problem idea from Kindergarten (k-add-sub-stories-10).

corrections.title: Any order, zero, and checking
corrections.reason: Read aloud, the title 'Order, zero, and checking' sounds like the ordering-numbers skill (g1-compare-order-50, 'Compare and order to 50'). The skill is about the commutative property (adding in any order), so 'Any order' says what the skill teaches and avoids confusion.

output.notes: I checked all 13 Grade 1 skills for unneeded, indirect, or missing prerequisites, forward or self references, and kid-friendly wording. All prerequisite ids exist in the prompt, and none point to a later grade or to the skill itself. Corrections were made only where a listed prerequisite is clearly unneeded or a needed one is missing, plus one title whose wording is ambiguous when read aloud. Items I judged acceptable and left alone: g1-count-50 in g1-equal-groups and g1-estimate-50 (skip counting by 2s, 5s, and 10s), g1-add-sub-facts-10 (k-make-numbers-to-10 is already covered through k-add-sub-facts-5), and g1-compare-unit-fractions (g1-half-equals-two-fourths is needed for comparing halves and fourths). Fixing the ordering skill leaves the rest of the chain consistent.
